# Jira DC hardening — follow-on to e369

## Context

Epic [rebar:e369-a449-4773-48fb] delivered Jira Server/Data Center support and met its
operator-approved exit bar: the live DC harness green end to end (run **30964805133**: 62 passed,
1 xfailed, 0 failed, canary `collected=63 executed=62 skipped=1`), 58 descendants, 0 uncertified.

This epic holds the DC work discovered BY that delivery which is hardening rather than the feature
itself. It exists so no DC bug is left unparented while e369 closes on the scope it actually shipped.
Operator decision, 2026-08-05: allow e369 to close; continue hardening here.

## What is in scope

* [rebar:4a6d-5bbc-44f4-4a56] (bug) — the THIRD live-DC channel never got 9790's readiness rule.
  `.github/workflows/jira-dc-capability-map.yml` gates on the same cheap `serverInfo` curl loop, then
  runs the mapper whose job is to record the Epic-field ids as the DECLARED CONTRACT a human commits.
  Worse than the two channels already fixed, because it **reports rather than fails**: a fast run
  silently writes a WRONG contract instead of erroring.
* [rebar:a3fa-...] (bug) — capability call sites are cast but not runtime-guarded, so a non-capable
  transport fails silently.
* [rebar:f020-0960-2c42-4d61] (task) — decide the fate of the dormant absence-probe port
  (`probe_remote` / `SupportsAbsenceProbe` / `inbound_probe.py`) left dormant by 3b5f. **Blocked on an
  operator decision**, not on engineering: deleting it removes DC's only import of the shared
  `classify_probe_response`, which weakens e369 AC5's both-backends claim.

## Explicitly NOT in scope

Cloud-surface defects found by DC parity guards ([rebar:6194-...], [rebar:6a74-...],
[rebar:9a46-...]) — real, but Cloud's, not DC feature delivery. The general vacuous-guard class
([rebar:8a5e-b88e-0c3e-4544]) and capability-map trust infrastructure
([rebar:a9bd-6641-e603-42bc]) are tracked on their own tickets; a9bd was explicitly unparented by
operator instruction.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] 4a6d is fixed per its recorded OPERATOR DECISION (2026-08-12, option (a)): the capability-map
      workflow validates the Epic-field contract AFTER the agent run and marks the report
      UNVERIFIED / fails the job when the run cannot distinguish "the image lacks the Epic fields"
      from "no Software project existed yet". A pre-run `await_required_fields` gate is explicitly
      OUT of scope — that is the pre-create call site bug 941b landed to REMOVE and
      `scripts/jira_dc_field_readiness.py` bans in terms; the capability-map `main()` creates no
      project before the agent run, so the wait would deadlock and burn its budget every run. The
      exact discriminator predicate and the inventory it reads are 4a6d's to specify and are
      deliberately not fixed here (epic altitude); the shared readiness module stays the single
      source of the field contract across all THREE live-DC channels, consulted after the run
      rather than awaited before it
- [ ] the map run FAILS rather than reports when the contract cannot be established — proven by a test
      that pins a system-only inventory as not-ready on that surface, not merely by configuration
- [ ] a3fa is fixed: capability casts are runtime-guarded so a non-capable transport fails loudly
      rather than silently, with a test that pins the loud failure
- [ ] f020 is decided and the decision recorded with its reason, including what it does to e369 AC5's
      both-backends claim on `classify_probe_response`
- [ ] the live DC harness is still GREEN end to end after this epic's changes (0 failed cells) —
      inherited from e369's exit bar, so hardening cannot regress the delivered feature
- [ ] no cell is deleted, skipped or `xfail`ed to reach green (the standing operator constraint)

## Testing

    gh workflow run "Live External Integration" --ref main    # the live DC harness
    pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 4 --dist worksteal -q
    make lint && make typecheck
